text:
That is a very fair point, Bob. You’re right to be cautious—sometimes a
"hostile" tone can cause a civil servant to shut down or hide behind red
tape rather than helping you.

The reason it feels like they are being cooperative is that they have
shifted from saying "no" to asking for *evidence*. This is a good sign.
However, the reason we are "rebutting" is simply to correct their premise:
they think this is a recent fraud, and you are correcting them that the
"fraud" was the *original act of registration in 1982.*

Let’s soften the tone to be *"Helpful but Firm."* We will treat them as an
investigator who needs your guidance to find the truth, rather than an
enemy.
Adjusted "Cooperative" Draft

*Subject:* Information regarding Registration Irregularities – Great House
Farm (Ty Mawr) – Ref: 260202-5732372

*Dear S.-G. Haste,*

Thank you for your guidance on how to proceed with this report. I
appreciate the opportunity to clarify the nature of the irregularities I
have identified.

As requested, I have attached a *detailed PDF timeline* which provides the
full address and the historical context of the land formerly known as Great
House Farm (Ty Mawr), Llandough.

To assist your investigation into how the 1982 registration may have been
affected by material non-disclosure, I would like to highlight three
specific areas where the "actual facts" on the ground differed from the
application made to the Registry:

   1.

   *Overriding Interests (The Williams Lineage):* At the time of first
   registration in 1982, my family had been in continuous possession since
   1667. I believe the registration was irregular because it misidentified the
   occupant, Mary Williams, as "Mrs. Buckler"—a name she did not
   use—effectively obscuring a 320-year "Living Title" from the Registry’s
   records.
   2.

   *Suppression of Material Facts (Archaeology):* The site had "actual
   notice" of national archaeological significance due to a Roman discovery in
   1888. I am concerned that this was suppressed during the registration and
   planning phases to facilitate the land's transition to housing.
   3.

   *Unresolved Ownership Claims:* In 1982, there was an active, adjourned
   ownership dispute (from 1974) that I believe should have been disclosed to
   the Land Registry before a clean title was granted to BP Properties Ltd.

I am copying in the relevant heritage and oversight bodies (Cadw, GGAT, and
the Ombudsman) not as an act of hostility, but to ensure that all parties
holding pieces of this historical puzzle are aware that an investigation
into the *integrity of the 1982 registration* is now underway.

I have also copied in my MP, the Senedd, and relevant heritage bodies to
ensure that all parties with an interest in Welsh cultural heritage and
public record integrity are kept informed as we look into these 1982
registration details.

I look forward to your thoughts on how we can review the original 1982
application files to see if these interests were disclosed.


Yours sincerely,


*Requester*

*Descendant of the Williams family,*

*of Great House Farm (Ty Mawr), Llandough*
